I think there's a little confusion here over some linguistic semantics.

**Sovereignty** is just the ability of a political body to have final and exclusive say over how the people inside their borders are governed, without interference/assault from outside those borders. It's something a nation can have more or less of, but makes no judgement about the morality or ethics of that governance or the origin of that political body. It's solely concerned with internal Vs external rule.

The horrible political body controlling Iran have low Sovereignty. The reasonably-decent political body controlling Ukraine also has low Sovereignty. Neither has zero, because that only happens when a country is conquered or collapses.

What Ukraine has much more of than Iran is **Legitimacy**. The ruling body of Ukraine was elected in relatively fair elections. The ruling body of Iran has been committing crimes against humanity on its own citizens. Legitimacy is explicitly a moral/ethical judgement.

Possession of nuclear weapons allow a state of any Legitimacy to maintain Sovereignty. For good or ill.
